text:
alex: heads up — seeing a dashboard regression in canary after last frontend rollout. charts taking forever to paint :eyes: p50 chart_render_ms went from ~120ms to ~520ms.

maria: ugh. did we change any bundle split / lazy import heuristics in that deploy?

alex: yep, I landed a small tweak to the module-splitter to inline a shared util for tile rendering (thought it would reduce roundtrips). diff: `modules/tiles/renderer.ts -> moved getTileKey into common/renderer-utils`

jon: was that the same PR that bumped the charting lib to v3.2.1? iirc there was an import path change that forced a bigger chunk.

alex: it did include the chart patch. bundle analyzer shows +92KB parsed JS in main bundle for the metrics pane.

ray: telemetry shows correlated parse/compile spikes on the client: `telemetry.chart.parse_time.p50: 110ms -> 480ms` around the rollout time. also spike in telemetry ingestion (sample rate *should* be same).

sophie: deploy-bot: can you paste the deploy id and canary percentage?

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T22:13Z (id: d-2026-0317-2213), canary 10% -> rolled to 25% at 22:40, no automated rollback triggered.

maria: thanks. hypothesis: the new module inlined a heavy dependency that used dynamic Intl/polyfill code path which triggers bigger parse. or we regressed lazy loading so chart chunks land in main.

jon: quick repro steps: load /dashboard?canary=1 in EU canary, open devtools -> Performance -> reload with throttling off. check "Main thread > Scripting" and "Parsed JS". I see long parse tasks ~300-700ms.

alex: i ran that and captured a flamegraph. root cause shows a single file parse: `chunk-main-tiles-abc123.js` responsible for most of the time.

ray: network waterfall shows chunk loaded earlier (prefetch changed?), and then parse blocked rendering. any change to prefetch/push heuristics recently?

maria: yes — PR #4882 adjusted prefetch priority to try to kickstart LCP for heavy dashboards. looks like it inadvertently promoted the tiles chunk into the critical path.

sophie: can we patch to demote that chunk again and move the util back to the tile module (fast revert)? that'll reintroduce the extra network hop but keeps parse off critical path.

alex: i can make the revert PR now. do we want immediate rollback of the canary expansion?

jon: yes, pause rollout at 25% and hold. open a rollback ticket. also we should add a quick E2E check: measure parsed JS per route in canary smoke.

maria: adding metric to rollout gate: `canary.parsed_js_main_bytes` and `canary.main_parse_time_p50`. gate threshold: no >50% increase vs baseline.

ray: also add a client-side sampled marker so we can trace which chunk caused parse: `window.__rw_chunk_marker = { activeChunk: 'tiles-v2' }` — small patch.

deploy-bot: action: canary expansion paused by ops (ticket #INC-7621).

alex: created PR #4921 (revert module move + demote prefetch) — includes a small perf test in /test/perf/compare-parsed-js.sh:
```
# run from root
yarn start:canary && curl -s "http://canary.internal/dashboard" | grep "chunk-main-tiles" || true
```

maria: can we get a quick QA run on EU canary and a perf snapshot? sophie, jon — can you validate?

sophie: on it. i'll run through the perf steps and post screenshots.

jon: i'll wire the rollout gate metric into the console so future expansions auto-block if parsed JS or parse time spikes.

ray: also file a small infra follow-up: revert changed prefetch heuristic or make it route-aware (don't prefetch tiles chunk for initial metric pane load).

alex: thanks team. next steps: (1) hold canary expansion, (2) apply revert PR, (3) QA perf smoke, (4) resume if metrics green. assigning: alex -> PR, sophie -> QA, jon -> rollout gate.

maria: and add a short postmortem note in #postmortems after we finish — include heap/parse numbers + chunk mapping. :memo:

sophie: quick note: reproducible locally in ~30s, i got p50 parse down to ~150ms after revert locally. will report back with traces. :white_check_mark:
